sources.entry: Swifty - Free and offline password manager.

summary.one_liner: Rowel (repo name swifty) is a free, open-source, offline-first password and secrets manager that stores encrypted vaults on your own devices, with optional sync through your own Google Drive, Dropbox or iCloud.
keywords: store passwords on my own devices
summary.what_it_does: Rowel stores logins, passkeys, TOTP codes, credit cards, identities, documents, secure notes, file attachments, SSH keys, API keys and whole .env files in an encrypted vault. The vault is split into lockboxes (for example Personal or Work), each kept as an encrypted SQLCipher database on the local device, with each item sealed again at the application layer. Optional sync uploads each lockbox as one encrypted file to Google Drive, Dropbox or iCloud, and edits from different devices merge per item. It can import from 1Password, LastPass, Bitwarden, KeePass CSV, Enpass, Chrome, Safari and FIDO CXF exports, and export to CSV, FIDO CXF, or Bitwarden-compatible JSON. Browser autofill and passkeys are offered for Chrome, Edge, Brave, Vivaldi, Firefox and Safari, and iOS AutoFill is included. The README also describes AI agent grants, time-limited encrypted item sharing links, Vault Health checks, and a command line tool.
use_cases: keep SSH keys and .env files secret
sync an encrypted vault across devices with my own cloud
share a single login securely by expiring link
how_to_run: Download the installer for your platform from the releases page (.dmg, setup .exe, .deb/.rpm/.AppImage, or TestFlight on iOS)
Build from source: git clone && cd rowel
notable: No account and no backend server; vault lives in encrypted files on your own disk and works offline
Each item is encrypted a second time inside the vault, so list and search run without unsealing secrets
Developer item types for SSH keys (Ed25519 generation in-app), API keys with scopes, and whole .env files
Releases ship SLSA build provenance, and desktop auto-updates only install minisign-signed updates
Private sharing by link that expires in 24 hours and can be revoked
caveats: Windows and Linux installers are not code-signed yet; verify with build provenance instead
iOS is distributed only through Apple TestFlight while in beta
iCloud sync on Mac depends on the build carrying Apple's iCloud entitlement
A paid tier for professional teams is mentioned as a possible future option; the README says the free app will not lose features
Building from source requires Bun and the Tauri/Rust toolchain, plus extra setup described in docs/development.md for iOS and Google OAuth
